evidence: The Fear & Greed Index plummeted to 10 ('Extreme Fear') on 2025-11-15, down 6 points from 16 and well below both the 7-day average (20.29) and 30-day average (29.33). While extreme fear reflects severe negative market sentiment and ongoing selling pressure, historic readings reaching near-single-digit levels frequently trigger technical relief bounces and short-term mean-reversion buying over a 24-hour horizon. Consequently, a mild contrarian upward tilt is favored, balanced against the risk of continued capitulation momentum.
limitations: Fear and Greed is a lagging composite sentiment metric and does not account for real-time intraday order-book flow or unexpected macroeconomic events.
Extreme fear regimes can persist and undergo further downward price discovery prior to any sustainable reversal.
Snapshot availability and later revisions are caller-attested, not independently verified.
